tab1.role_description: A junior .NET Developer in India builds ASP.NET Core web APIs, writes C# business logic and LINQ queries, creates Entity Framework database models, and writes unit tests using NUnit or xUnit. Their week includes fixing defects in Visual Studio, reviewing code in Azure DevOps or GitHub, attending sprint ceremonies, and deploying services to Azure or on-premises Windows servers. .NET roles are prominent in IT services companies delivering to US and UK banking and insurance clients, as well as in companies building Windows-based enterprise software.

tab1.role_description: An AI Engineer in India builds AI-powered applications and systems — developing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, AI agent architectures, LLM-powered APIs, and intelligent automation solutions using foundation models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and others. This is a rapidly growing role in India, reflecting the shift from traditional ML model-building toward AI application development using foundation models. AI Engineers work in product companies, GCCs, AI-focused startups, and IT services firms building AI-enabled solutions for enterprise clients.
tab1.narrative_para1: An AI Engineer in India builds AI-powered applications and systems — developing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, AI agent architectures, LLM-powered APIs, and intelligent automation solutions using foundation models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and others. This is a rapidly growing role in India, reflecting the shift from traditional ML model-building toward AI application development using foundation models. AI Engineers work in product companies, GCCs, AI-focused startups, and IT services firms building AI-enabled solutions for enterprise clients.
tab1.narrative_para2: AI Engineers work with AI tools as core infrastructure — OpenAI API (GPT-4o), Anthropic Claude API, and GitHub Copilot are central to their daily workflow. RAG pipelines, AI agent frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex), and vector databases can be substantially built using AI-assisted development. ChatGPT and Claude assist with system prompt design, API integration debugging, and documentation. This is an AI-Evolving role with among the highest AI exposure in the sector — the tools are the product. The human value — AI system architecture decisions, hallucination risk management, and responsible deployment governance — requires deep practical expertise.
tab1.narrative_para3: AI Engineering suits people who are excited by the pace of LLM capability development and want to build practical AI applications using foundation models. If you enjoy working with cutting-edge AI tools, have strong software engineering skills, and are motivated by building AI systems that real users rely on — this is a fast-moving, high-demand career track. Python, REST API development, and familiarity with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face) are the core entry skills; LangChain/LlamaIndex and vector database experience (Pinecone, Weaviate) build rapidly through project work.

tab1.role_description: An AML (Anti-Money Laundering) Analyst in India investigates suspicious financial transactions, monitors for money laundering and terrorist financing activity, and ensures compliance with PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act) and RBI/IRDAI AML guidelines. Core work includes reviewing transaction monitoring alerts, conducting Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) on high-risk customers, investigating layering and integration patterns, filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with FIU-IND, and supporting regulatory examination responses. AML Analysts work in the compliance and financial crime functions of banks, insurance companies, NBFCs, stockbrokers, and payment companies.
tab1.narrative_para1: An AML (Anti-Money Laundering) Analyst in India investigates suspicious financial transactions, monitors for money laundering and terrorist financing activity, and ensures compliance with PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act) and RBI/IRDAI AML guidelines. Core work includes reviewing transaction monitoring alerts, conducting Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) on high-risk customers, investigating layering and integration patterns, filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with FIU-IND, and supporting regulatory examination responses. AML Analysts work in the compliance and financial crime functions of banks, insurance companies, NBFCs, stockbrokers, and payment companies.
tab1.narrative_para2: AI-powered transaction monitoring systems automate suspicious activity detection, PEP/sanctions screening, and Currency Transaction Report threshold alerts. ChatGPT and Claude assist with interpreting PMLA regulations, FIU-IND guidance, and drafting STR narratives. Insurance KYC and proposal processing is increasingly AI-assisted through automated document verification. This is an AI-Evolving role with high AI exposure on automated detection and screening — the irreplaceable human value, investigating complex layering schemes involving Indian informal financial networks, benami transactions, and hawala connections, and applying PMLA accountability in STR filings, requires deep contextual knowledge and professional judgment.
tab1.narrative_para3: AML Analysis suits people with strong investigative instincts, genuine interest in financial crime patterns and money laundering typologies, and the professional discipline for the rigorous documentation standards that regulatory accountability requires. If you can identify patterns in financial transaction data that indicate suspicious behaviour, understand India's informal finance ecosystem including hawala and benami structures, and can write clear, legally defensible investigation narratives — this is a growing and respected specialisation. CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist) certification is the most valued professional credential for AML careers in India's financial services market.
